method.scanner: skan.py masks comments and string/raw literals, rebuilds function scopes by braces (586 functions), finds open/remove/rename/exists with a file name, and records which lock primitives appear in the enclosing body
method.failure_mode: any change of the firmware without updating the report fails the check on purpose

findings.single_writer: historiaFlushDoFS() -> historiaIo.append(Stream::Short/Long, ...) under logMutex; no direct open(...,"a") anywhere
findings.startup_readers: historiaWczytajZFS() and historiaDlugaWczytajZFS() run before the history task is created, so they are single threaded
findings.runtime_readers: sendTelegramDocumentHistKrotka() and sendTelegramDocumentHistDluga() open the file with no lock and no pin and stream it to Telegram; the call site has no logMutex in a +-25 line window
findings.http_endpoints: /api/history and /api/history/long serve RAM buffers, not the file
findings.clear_disabled: historiaWyczysc() returns false without touching the filesystem, so there is no runtime rotation today
findings.editor_blocked: historiaChronionaSciezka() rejects the history paths and the A1 request files

risk: The two Telegram readers are safe only by accident: append-only file plus a prefix length taken from cache. They break when rotation returns, and they can announce a Content-Length larger than the bytes they actually read.
The download route from 209 must go through the 207 pin; those two senders are its natural clients.
not_qualified: no firmware was run: LittleFS, WDT, RAM and timing behaviour are not proven
only history files were analysed; logs and settings were not
a missing lock in a function is a static fact, not a proof about all call paths
the 586 function count comes from a brace heuristic, not a full C++ parser
